item.title: More nice things for this blog
item.description:
I continue to improve this website to make it a better representation of me on the Internet.

In the past year and a half, I have:

  • added dark mode support. I myself use dark mode exclusively at work, so it was long overdue.
  • revamped the reviews. This section grew unwieldy over time, and needed a better structure.
  • added a ’lists’ section. More things about me, with nice Mermaid timelines.
  • added a ‘DIY’ section. A simple gallery of things I’ve built over the years.
  • added site-wide search. Easy way to search this website without ripgrep.

This time I added a few more things (all made easy thanks to Hugo).

item.title: Added search
item.description:
After 13 years of blogging, this blog grew relatively big.

At least big enough that I myself can’t always remember what I wrote about, and where.

The solution is of course obvious - just add a search feature!

However, this is a statically generated website.

All the pages are converted from Markdown to HTML by Hugo and pushed to Github Pages.

Which means there is no backend that normally runs the search for us.

item.title: Moving from Pelican to Hugo for this blog
item.description:
Since I no longer enjoy working with Python in any shape or form, it was only a matter of time (mostly a matter of my free time) for this to happen. I’ve migrated this blog from Pelican static site generator (written in Python) to Hugo (written in Go).

It by no means reflects on Pelican as a piece of software (it’s actually pretty good). It’s more about my disdain for Python, and awesome experience I had with Hugo and Go language in general.

item.title: My new Scale Models gallery
item.description:
I’ve just published my new site - personal Scale Models Gallery.

Model making is my main and favorite hobby, so I’ve decided to build a whole new site just to write about it.

I just love doing something without the computer, it’s an awesome way to de-stress and detox.

Also I love to make notes about things I do, read, watch or play. And one day I’ve just realized that I want to turn my notes about making scale models with all this wip photos and comments about quality or tools into something bigger.
